text:
Filip Chytil is playing big minutes for a Vancouver team that can't keep the puck. He's back in the lineup since Nov. 13 after a two-week gap in his game log, and he's averaging 19:22 a night, the most of his career by a distance. With him on the ice at five on five, the Canucks get only 31% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), more than eleven points worse than when he sits. That's a hard number to defend, even accounting for linemates Evolving-Hockey rated among the league's weakest last season.

The scoring has been fine. Four goals in his last six games, including two against Vegas on Nov. 15, and his finishing matches his chances. Nov. 22 against Chicago showed both sides in one night: Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis called it "a dreadful start" (a giveaway and a penalty on his first two shifts led to goals) before Chytil scored on a fortunate bounce.

Fourteen games is a small sample. Watch the five-on-five share; at 19 minutes a night, it decides a lot of Canucks games.
